syllabus_topics: Relevance of Fluid Mechanics in Engineering
Continuum Assumption. Material System
Definition of Fluid. Viscosity. Newtonian and Non-Newtonian Fluids. Newton's Law. Turbulence and Reynolds Number
Fundamental Laws of Fluid Mechanics
Fundamental Equation of Fluid Statics
Fluid Statics under gravity. Hydrostatic Equation
Forces on surfaces
Types of Fluid Flow Analysis
Lagrangian and Eulerian Descriptions
The Eulerian Description. The Reynolds Transport Theorem
Integral Form of Mass Conservation. Compressible and Incompressible Flow. Mean Velocity, Flow Rate and Average Density
Integral Form of Momentum Equation. Average Velocity and Momentum-Flux Correction Factor
Integral Form of the Energy Equation. Bernoulli's Equation. Head Losses. Head Losses in Pipes. Fluid Machinery
Limitations of Integral Flow Analysis. Scope of Differential Flow Analysis
Differential Equations of Fluid Mechanics. Navier-Stokes Equations for Incompressible Flows
Fully Developed Flows
Introduction to Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD)
Mathematical Modeling of a Hydraulic System
Valves
Calculation, Dimensioning and Regulation of Hydraulic Systems
teaching_methods: Individual or group work, problem solving and laboratory reports
Personal interview with the course instructor
Personal study (Theoretical content study, Problem solving)
assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, the assessment includes a Final Exam (72%), a Topic 1 test (3%), Laboratory Practices and report (10%), a Topic 4 Ansys-Fluent Practice (10%), and Student Participation (5%). The Topic 4 Practice grade (C) is obtained by C=Np·m, where Np is the practice note and m depends on the grade obtained in the Topic 4 problem of the Final Exam. Two liberatory tests for Topics 2 and 3 allow students to secure a minimum of 60% for the corresponding sections of the final exam, with the option to retake and keep the higher grade. For the extraordinary call, grades of 50% or more in Laboratory Practices and Ansys-Fluent Practice are carried over, but liberatory tests and Topic 1 evaluation are only valid for the ordinary call.
